claim: Disabling FMA at compile time raises stock CMP 170HX FP32 throughput from ~0.39 TFLOPS to ~6.2 TFLOPS, a 15x recovery that reaches about half the card's theoretical FP32.
stance_target: The community workaround the repo relies on to make the card usable for compute at all
scope_conditions: CMP 170HX 8 GB over Oculink x4, Ryzen 7 7840HS host, driver 570.86.16, CUDA 12.8, -fmad=false builds
quoted_support: By default, the FP32 performance of the 170HX is remarkably low, at approximately 0.39 TFLOPS ... when applying a suggestion from user niconini's blog post - specifically, disabling Fused Multiply-Add (FMA) instructions during compilation - the CMP 170HX can achieve approximately 6.2 TFLOPS in benchmarks, reaching half of its theoretical FP32 performance.

claim: FP16 throughput is unaffected by the FMA setting and reaches roughly 42 TFLOPS in OpenCL/mixbench, but PyTorch and gpu-burn report only ~6.3 TFLOPS FP16.
stance_target: The assumption that PyTorch can exploit the card's FP16 capability without further work - a precondition for any PyTorch training experiment
scope_conditions: Stock CMP 170HX 8 GB, PyTorch and gpu-burn versus OpenCL/mixbench, no tensor-core kernels exercised
quoted_support: The FP16 performance of the nVidia CMP 170HX remains unaffected regardless of FMA status ... However, the FP16 performance reported by PyTorch and GPU-Burn is only around 6.3 TFLOPS, which is significantly lower than the results from OpenCL-Benchmark and Mixbench.

claim: On the stock card Tensor Cores cannot be used for acceleration, which is why llama.cpp prefill reaches only 14-45% of the A100-scaled theoretical estimate.
stance_target: The repo's measured 162 TFLOPS bf16 per GPU, which implies working tensor-core paths on the unlocked card
scope_conditions: Stock CMP 170HX 8 GB, llama-bench on Qwen2.5-1.5B at multiple quantisations, FMA disabled
quoted_support: Even with FMA disabled, prefill speeds only reached 14-45% of theoretical limits. This discrepancy likely stems from the inability to utilize Tensor Cores for acceleration.

claim: Decode throughput reaches 39-78% of the bandwidth-scaled theoretical estimate, consistent with decode being memory-bandwidth-bound rather than compute-bound.
stance_target: The repo's premise that the card's retained HBM2e bandwidth is its usable asset
scope_conditions: Stock CMP 170HX 8 GB, llama-bench decode on Qwen2.5-1.5B, scaling from A100 measured bandwidth
quoted_support: since memory bandwidth is not a bottleneck, it achieves 39-78% of theoretical performance. Disabling FMA further boosts decoding speeds for quantized models (Q8/Q6_K/Q4_K_M/Q2_K_M), reaching 50-78% of theoretical performance.

claim: The CMP 170HX natively supports PCIe 1.1 x4; populating the missing coupling capacitors would theoretically give x16 but the author did not validate it.
stance_target: The repo's claim that link width is a hardware (solder) mod separate from the software Gen2 patch
scope_conditions: Stock card, Oculink x4 connection, no hardware modification attempted
quoted_support: The CMP 170HX natively supports PCIe 1.1 x4 bandwidth. By populating additional coupling capacitors on the PCB, the interface can theoretically operate at PCIe 1.1 x16, though this modification was not validated in this study.
numbers: PCIe 1.1 x16 theoretical after cap population

claim: The card is GA100-105F-A1 with 70 SMs, 4480 CUDA cores and 280 Tensor Cores at a 250 W TDP, with 8 GB HBM2e at 1493 GB/s.
stance_target: The hardware specification table in the repo's documentation
scope_conditions: Derived from TechPowerUp GPU database and scaled from A100 documentation, since Nvidia published no whitepaper
quoted_support: GPU Name NVIDIA CMP 170HX ... GPU Codename GA100-105F-A1 ... CUDA Cores 4480 ... Streaming Multiprocessors 70 ... Tensor Cores 280 ... TDP 250 W ... Memory Size 8 GB ... Memory Bandwidth 1493 GB/s

claim: Theoretical performance of the card is 50.53 TFLOPS FP16, 12.63 TFLOPS FP32 and 6.317 TFLOPS FP64, with INT32 uncapped at 12.5 TIOPS.
stance_target: Whether the repo's ~162 TFLOPS bf16/GPU measurement is physically plausible for a 70-SM GA100
scope_conditions: Scaled from A100 SM count (108) to CMP 170HX SM count (70) at the same boost clock
quoted_support: Boost FP16 Performance 50.53 TFLOPS ... Boost FP32 Performance 12.63 TFLOPS ... Boost FP64 Performance 6.317 TFLOPS

claim: FP64 performance is 1/64 of theoretical peak and drops to 1/128 when FMA is disabled, with no known recovery method.
stance_target: The repo's decision to run everything in bf16 and never rely on fp64
quoted_support: The FP64 performance of the CMP 170HX is approximately 1/64 of its theoretical peak performance, and this drops to 1/128 when FMA (Fused Multiply-Add) is disabled.

claim: Energy efficiency matches the A100 only when the workload is memory-bandwidth-bound, and disabling FMA improves quantised decode speed but lowers energy efficiency.
stance_target: Whether the box is a good tokens-per-watt proposition for training versus inference
scope_conditions: llama-bench decode on Qwen2.5-1.5B, power via nvidia-smi, single card
quoted_support: The CMP 170HX achieves energy efficiency comparable to the A100 only when the bottleneck of an application (e.g., LLM inference) is memory bandwidth. Disabling FMA improves decoding speed for quantized models (e.g., Q6, Q4_K_M) but reduces energy efficiency.

claim: The study's test platform was a single card over Oculink x4 on a Ryzen 7 7840HS mini-PC, so it measures one card in isolation and says nothing about multi-GPU collectives.
stance_target: Whether this paper can adjudicate the repo's multi-GPU DDP/EP/TP claims
scope_conditions: Single-GPU test bench, Debian 12.9, kernel 6.1.0-31, driver 570.86.16, CUDA 12.8
quoted_support: Due to experimental constraints, the GPU was tested via an Oculink-connected PCIe interface on a custom-built mini-PC platform.

claim: The author identifies three theoretical routes to full performance recovery: cracking the driver, open-source driver stacks, or hand-written CUDA that avoids FMA, and judges PyTorch modification impractical because of its size.
stance_target: The repo's implicit bet that a patched driver (cmpunlocker) plus a custom training harness is the viable path, not stock PyTorch
quoted_support: PyTorch's massive codebase complicates manual adjustments to its CUDA-level FMA dependencies. ... Custom CUDA programming: Developing standalone CUDA programs (instead of relying on PyTorch) could fully utilize the CMP 170HX's 50 TFLOPS FP16 and 6 TFLOPS FP32 performance

claim: The card's VRAM capacity of 8 GB is the binding constraint for LLM work in the stock configuration, forcing the study down to a 1.5B model.
stance_target: The repo's claim that the 64 GB unlock is what makes 7B-class work possible at all
scope_conditions: Stock 8 GB card, llama.cpp with all layers offloaded
quoted_support: Considering the nVidia CMP 170HX has only 8GB HBM2e memory, we selected the Qwen2.5-1.5B model to ensure all layers of LLM weights could be loaded into GPU VRAM.
